OWNING AN ARENA

On the Foundation zone (5.161.238.245:5000, Continuum or oss-client) any player can ask for an arena of their own. If staff say yes, the arena is yours: you choose its settings, its map and its graphics, and you can pick up to five co-mods to help run it. Everything is public: who asked for what, who decided, and why.

First: claim your name

Foundation has its own accounts (there is no billing server). Every player needs one: the zone only lets in names that have been claimed, and making an arena and arena powers only work for a logged-in name. To claim yours:

  1. Go to subspacefoundation.com/account/signup and enter your name, a password (8 to 31 characters) and a recovery email. We email you a 6-digit code; enter it and the name is yours. It's first come, first served.
  2. In game, log in with that same name and password. That makes you logged in, which you need to make or own an arena or to use ?weblogin.
  3. Forgot your password? Use subspacefoundation.com/account/forgot: we email a code to your recovery email and you choose a new password. You can also change your password and email while signed in on the site.

If you played here before: your old name and password still work in game. The first time you sign in on the site with your old name and password, you will be asked to add a recovery email (we send a code to confirm it). Until you do, you can't recover the account if you forget the password.

If a login says "This name isn't claimed", this is the step you are missing. Passwords are changed on the site.

Making an arena

Type, in any arena:

?makearena <name> [what the arena is for]

for example ?makearena skyrace Fast racing laps for warbirds. Or use Make an arena in your hub. There is no approval: the arena is yours at once.

  • The name is 3 to 15 characters of lowercase letters and digits. It must start with a letter and must not end in a digit. Names already in use (and public, 2v2pub, 3v3pub, 4v4pub, duel) are taken.
  • The description is optional, up to 120 characters. Everyone can read it.
  • You can own one arena at a time. ?requestarena still works and does the same thing.

Then go to your arena with ?go <name>. Staff can still suspend an arena that breaks the rules.

What owners and co-mods can do

In your own arena (the powers do not work anywhere else):

  • Owner: change settings (?arenaset or the web page), upload the map and graphics, pick co-mods, and the moderator tools below.
  • Co-mods (up to 5): change settings and use the moderator tools. They cannot upload files or change who the co-mods are.
  • Moderator tools (both): arena messages (?a), the game timer, locking or recycling the arena, flags and balls, setting players' ships and teams, prizes, spectating, and chat masks. Kicks, bans and zone-wide messages stay with zone staff.

Commands

For everyone

CommandWhat it does
?makearena <name> [pitch]Make an arena of your own, right away (needs a password, see above).
?arenarequestsLists the newest arenas (and any requests from before arenas launched without approval).
?arenalog [name]The last 10 public events (requests, decisions, co-mod changes, …), for all arenas or one.
?myarenaShows the arena you own: status, co-mods, when someone last entered it.
?webloginSends you a one-time link to the arena web page (valid 10 minutes, works once).

Owners and co-mods, in their own arena

CommandWhat it does
?arenaset <Section:Key> <value>Change one setting, e.g. ?arenaset Warbird:BulletSpeed 3000.
?arenaget <Section:Key>Show the current value of one setting.

Owners only, in their own arena

CommandWhat it does
?comodLists your co-mods.
?comod add <player> / ?comod remove <player>Adds or removes a co-mod (public in ?arenalog). A new co-mod must have an account (claimed at subspacefoundation.com/account/signup).
?arenamap <file.lvl>Uploads a map from your Continuum folder; it becomes the arena's map.
?putlvz <file.lvz>Uploads a graphics file from your Continuum folder and adds it to the arena. Uploading a file with the same name as one already there replaces it.
?rmlvz <file.lvz>Removes a graphics file from the arena (and deletes it).

Staff

CommandWhat it does
?approvearena <name>Approves a request: creates the arena and makes the asker its owner (moderators and up).
?declinearena <name> <reason>Declines a request; the reason is public (moderators and up). Nobody can approve or decline their own request.
?arenaadmin suspend <name> <reason>Closes an arena to players (super moderators and sysops).
?arenaadmin revive <name>Reopens a suspended or archived arena.
?arenaadmin transfer <name> <player>Gives the arena to another player (a name with a Foundation account).
?arenaadmin archive <name>Closes the arena at once; its folder is stored away at the next server restart (nothing is deleted).

To take an arena or its powers away from an owner, use ?arenaadmin (suspend, transfer or archive). Removing the owner's group with ?rmgroup does not last: the module grants it again the next time they enter their arena.

Staff who own or co-mod an arena keep their own staff group there; their staff group already has the owner commands, which still work only in the arena they own (or co-mod).

Uploads with ?arenamap/?putlvz need Continuum (it sends the file). With any other client, use the web page.

The web page

Type ?weblogin in game. You get a link like https://subspacefoundation.com/arena/login?t=…. Open it within 10 minutes; it works once and signs you in for 24 hours. No password is ever typed on the web.

  • Everyone can see the public page, subspacefoundation.com/arena/: every player-owned arena with its owner, co-mods and players online, waiting requests, decisions and the public log.
  • Without an arena, the signed-in page launches one (same rules as ?makearena).
  • Owners and co-mods see their arena's settings, grouped by section, with a description, default and range for each, and can change them.
  • Owners can also upload the map (.lvl) and graphics (.lvz) by drag-and-drop, and remove a graphics file with its remove button. A graphics file with the same name as one already there replaces it.

Limits

  • One arena per player, and one waiting request per player.
  • Up to 5 co-mods per arena.
  • Map: one .lvl per arena, at most 2 MB.
  • Graphics: .lvz files of at most 5 MB each, at most 10 per arena. Replacing a file keeps its slot; ?rmlvz (or the web page) frees one.
  • Settings: at most 20 changes per minute per arena (in game and web together). Modules settings can't be changed, and the map and graphics lists change only through uploads.
  • An arena nobody enters for 30 days is archived (never while players are in it): it closes and its files are stored away at the next server restart, not deleted. Staff can bring it back with ?arenaadmin revive.
  • Every decision (request, approval, decline, transfer, suspend, revive, archive, co-mod change) is public in ?arenalog and on the web page.
